- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent mean), model often overshoots — cap next period’s forecast at +5% above prior peak.
- If sentiment turns positive mid-horizon (e.g., +0.3+), model frequently underreacts — adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for next 3–5 periods.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >15% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per period until convergence.
- Lagged sentiment: if sentiment was negative 3–5 days ago, model often underpredicts downward movement — add 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate volatility — reduce final 3–5 periods by 2–4% to match true outcome volatility.
